title: Admin
lead: Read-only. Every figure here traces to a query, and nothing on this page can change anything.
readOnly: Read-only, and the last section is built. Nothing here writes, and there is no action on this page — a panel that can act on data is a second application, with permissions, audit trails and a blast radius.

health.title: Health
health.commitAgree: Both services are running the same commit.
health.commitDisagree: The two services are running different commits — a deploy is half-finished, or one of them failed.
health.commitUnknown: Cannot tell whether the two agree: one is down, or neither was deployed from git.

players.title: Players
players.guests: {count, plural, =0 {no guests} one {# guest besides} other {# guests besides}}
players.ofAccounts: of {count, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}}
players.nobody: Nobody has finished a round yet.

activation.title: Activation
activation.activationWhy: Of the accounts created, the share that finished a round.
activation.returnWhy: Of those who finished a round, the share active on a later day.

why.created: Signed up. Guests are not counted — they are not accounts.
why.started: Pressed play at least once. Anybody missing here signed up and never began.
why.finished: Submitted at least one round. The gap above is rounds abandoned partway.
why.returned: Was active on a later day than their first. Two rounds in one sitting is not coming back.

activation.caveat: "Came back" is a later day of activity, not a cohort curve: a return the next day and a return six months on look the same here, because nothing records per-day history.

games.title: Games
games.abandonWhy: Of the seats in rounds that have ended, the share whose player never submitted.
games.caveat: Only rounds that have ended count towards the rate: a seat in a round still running has not abandoned anything. And it cannot be split by screen — typing a topic, voting and waiting for generation leave no row, so the split is by mode.

cost.title: Cost
cost.noRateWhy: No token rate is configured, so this section reports tokens rather than money. Set MODEL_INPUT_COST_PER_MTOK and MODEL_OUTPUT_COST_PER_MTOK to price them — a rate written into the repository would go stale without saying so.
cost.rateSet: Priced with the configured rate per million tokens.
cost.failed: {count, plural, one {# call failed and still cost tokens} other {# calls failed and still cost tokens}}
cost.withoutTokens: {count, plural, one {# call reported no token count} other {# calls reported no token count}} — the totals above are missing them.

content.title: Content
content.cacheWhy: A cached round costs nothing to generate, so this is what stands between a hundred rounds and a hundred generations.
content.ofGames: of {count, plural, one {# round} other {# rounds}}
content.ofCalls: of {count, plural, one {# call} other {# calls}}
content.topicFailures: {count, plural, =0 {No topic choice came back empty} one {# topic choice of {calls} came back empty} other {# topic choices of {calls} came back empty}} — a word Wikipedia has no article for is not a fault.
